thread:
Ellen (product): Quick nit on empty state for API keys when a user can't create keys in the org. Current mock shows a generic CTA 'Create API key' which confuses users without perms.
Marco (design): Agree. Propose two variants: (A) no keys + can_create -> primary CTA 'Create API key' with short explainer; (B) no keys + cannot_create -> explanatory copy + primary action 'Request access' (link) and a disabled 'Create API key' affordance.
Isha (backend): API can return a simple perms object: user_perms.can_create=false, can_request=true. We can surface a prefilled request link -> /orgs/:id/access-requests?type=key.
Tess (a11y): For the disabled button, ensure tooltip is keyboard-accessible and the reason is announced (aria-describedby). Also ensure the request link has an accessible name.
Rafi (content): Suggested copy for cannot_create: 'You don't have permission to create API keys. Request access from your org admin.' Button label: 'Request access'. Tooltip: 'Requires key.create permission.'
Marco (design): Visual notes: use a muted primary for disabled create, make the request action a clear link-style CTA, include a tiny help icon that opens a concise dialog explaining roles. Mobile: stack link then disabled button.
Ellen (product): Edge case: if user has existing keys but not create perms, show row-level actions but hide create. Provide a banner: 'You can use existing keys but cannot create new ones.'
ops-bot: Event logged -> EV-2223456-01, severity=info
Ellen (product): Action items: @Marco update mocks for both variants, @Rafi finalize microcopy, @Tess confirm a11y checklist, @Isha add perms flag to the API. Small patch next sprint. :ship:
